sanskrit: anuyātrikam arthasya mātrālābheṣv anādṛtaḥ alābhe na vihanyeta lābhaś cainaṃ na harṣayet
english: Indifferent to gain that merely sustains the body, content with the barest measure of alms, let him not be cast down when nothing comes, nor let any gain elate him.

sanskrit: lābhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ necchen na bhuñjītābhipūjitaḥ abhipūjitalābhaṃ hi jugupsetaiva tādṛśaḥ
english: Let him not desire a gain shared by many, nor eat what is given in homage to him; such a man should hold in disdain the alms offered out of reverence.

sanskrit: na cānnadoṣān nindeta na guṇān abhipūjayet śayyāsane vivikte ca nityam evābhipūjayet
english: Let him neither blame the faults of his food nor extol its merits; for his bed and seat let him ever esteem only what is solitary and apart.

sanskrit: śūnyāgāraṃ vṛkṣamūlam araṇyam atha vā guhām ajñātacaryāṃ gatvānyāṃ tato 'nyatraiva saṃviśet
english: An empty house, the foot of a tree, the forest, or a cave—having wandered there unknown, let him then dwell elsewhere again, ever moving on.

sanskrit: anurodhavirodhābhyāṃ samaḥ syād acalo dhruvaḥ sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ cobhe nānurudhyeta karmaṇi
english: Let him remain even-minded toward favor and opposition alike, unshaken and steadfast; let him be bound by neither the good deed nor the evil deed in his action.

sanskrit: vāco vegaṃ manasaḥ krodhavegaṃ; vivitsāvegam udaropasthavegam etān vegān vinayed vai tapasvī; nindā cāsya hṛdayaṃ nopahanyāt
english: The urge of speech, the urge of the mind, the urge of anger, the urge of curiosity, the urge of belly and loins—these urges the ascetic must subdue, and no reproach should wound his heart.

sanskrit: madhyastha eva tiṣṭheta praśaṃsānindayoḥ samaḥ etat pavitraṃ paramaṃ parivrājaka āśrame
english: Let him stand wholly neutral, even-minded amid praise and blame; this is the supreme purity in the order of the wandering mendicant.

sanskrit: mahātmā suvrato dāntaḥ sarvatraivānapāśritaḥ apūrvacārakaḥ saumyo aniketaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: Great-souled, firm in his vows, self-controlled, attached to nothing anywhere, walking paths he has never trodden before, gentle, homeless, and composed,

sanskrit: vānaprasthagṛhasthābhyāṃ na saṃsṛjyeta karhi cit ajñātalipsāṃ lipseta na cainaṃ harṣa āviśet
english: let him never consort with the forest-dweller or the householder; let him seek his alms from those who do not know him, and let no elation enter him.

sanskrit: vijānatāṃ mokṣa eṣa śramaḥ syād avijānatām mokṣayānam idaṃ kṛtsnaṃ viduṣāṃ hārito 'bravīt
english: For those who understand, this is liberation; for those who do not, it is mere toil. This whole vehicle of release belongs to the wise—so Hārita declared.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo dattvā yaḥ pravrajed gṛhāt lokās tejomayās tasya tathānantyāya kalpate
english: The man who, having granted freedom from fear to all beings, goes forth from his home—for him the worlds of radiance avail, and he attains to the infinite.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dhanyā dhanyā iti janāḥ sarve 'smān pravadanty uta na duḥkhitataraḥ kaś cit pumān asmābhir asti ha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Blessed, blessed!"—so all people proclaim us; yet there is surely no man more wretched in his grief than we are.

sanskrit: lokasaṃbhāvitair duḥkhaṃ yat prāptaṃ kurusattama prāpya jātiṃ manuṣyeṣu devair api pitāmaha
english: O best of the Kurus, the grief we have met, honored as we are by the world, came to us even though we were born among men by the will of the gods themselves, O grandsire.

sanskrit: kadā vayaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ saṃnyāsaṃ duḥkhasaṃjñakam duḥkham etac charīrāṇāṃ dhāraṇaṃ kurusattama
english: When shall we make our renunciation of this thing called sorrow? For the very bearing of these bodies is itself sorrow, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: vimuktāḥ saptadaśabhir hetubhūtaiś ca pañcabhiḥ indriyārthair guṇaiś caiva aṣṭābhiḥ prapitāmaha
english: Freed from the seventeen, and from the five that are their causes, and from the objects of the senses and from the eight qualities, O great-grandsire—

sanskrit: na gacchanti punarbhāvaṃ munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ kadā vayaṃ bhaviṣyāmo rājyaṃ hitvā paraṃtapa
english: the sages, rigorous in their vows, return no more to rebirth. When shall we, O scorcher of foes, become such, forsaking the kingdom?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nāsty anantaṃ mahārāja sarvaṃ saṃkhyānagocaram punarbhāvo 'pi saṃkhyāto nāsti kiṃ cid ihācalam
english: Bhīṣma said: Nothing is endless, O great king; all lies within the reach of reckoning. Even rebirth is numbered; nothing here is unchanging.

sanskrit: na cāpi gamyate rājan naiṣa doṣaḥ prasaṅgataḥ udyogād eva dharmajña kālenaiva gamiṣyatha
english: Yet that goal is not reached at will, O king, nor is this any fault that follows from circumstance. By earnest striving alone, O knower of dharma, and in due time, you shall reach it.

sanskrit: īśo 'yaṃ satataṃ dehī nṛpate puṇyapāpayoḥ tata eva samutthena tamasā rudhyate 'pi ca
english: This embodied soul is ever master of its own merit and demerit, O king; yet by the darkness that arises from those very deeds it is also bound and obstructed.

sanskrit: yathāñjanamayo vāyuḥ punar mānaḥśilaṃ rajaḥ anupraviśya tadvarṇo dṛśyate rañjayan diśaḥ
english: As the air, laden with collyrium's blackness, and again with the red dust of realgar, takes on that color as it enters them and is seen tinging the quarters of the sky,

sanskrit: tathā karmaphalair dehī rañjitas tamasāvṛtaḥ vivarṇo varṇam āśritya deheṣu parivartate
english: so the embodied soul, dyed by the fruits of its deeds and wrapped in darkness, though itself colorless, takes on a color and passes through one body after another.

sanskrit: jñānena hi yadā jantur ajñānaprabhavaṃ tamaḥ vyapohati tadā brahma prakāśeta sanātanam
english: For when a creature, through knowledge, dispels the darkness born of ignorance, then the eternal Brahman shines forth before it.

sanskrit: ayatnasādhyaṃ munayo vadanti; ye cāpi muktās ta upāsitavyāḥ tvayā ca lokena ca sāmareṇa; tasmān na śāmyanti maharṣisaṃghāḥ
english: The sages say that goal is attained without striving; and those who are liberated should be revered—by you, by the world, and by the gods together. Therefore the assemblies of great seers never cease from their endeavor.

sanskrit: asminn arthe purā gītaṃ śṛṇuṣvaikamanā nṛpa yathā daityena vṛtreṇa bhraṣṭaiśvaryeṇa ceṣṭitam
english: On this matter listen with single mind, O king, to what was sung of old—how the Daitya Vṛtra, fallen from his sovereignty, bore himself.

sanskrit: nirjitenāsahāyena hṛtarājyena bhārata aśocatā śatrumadhye buddhim āsthāya kevalām
english: Vanquished, without ally, his kingdom torn away, O Bhārata, yet grieving not amid his foes, resting upon understanding alone,

sanskrit: bhraṣṭaiśvaryaṃ purā vṛtram uśanā vākyam abravīt kaccit parājitasyādya na vyathā te 'sti dānava
english: to Vṛtra, fallen from his sovereignty, Uśanas of old spoke these words: "Surely now, O Dānava, defeated as you are, you feel no anguish?"

sanskrit: vṛtra uvāca satyena tapasā caiva viditvā saṃkṣayaṃ hy aham na śocāmi na hṛṣyāmi bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim
english: Vṛtra said: Having understood, through truth and through austerity, the perishing of all things, I neither grieve nor rejoice at the coming and going of beings.

sanskrit: kālasaṃcoditā jīvā majjanti narake 'vaśāḥ paridṛṣṭāni sarvāṇi divyāny āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Driven on by Time, helpless souls sink down into hell; the wise declare that all these divine realms have been fully seen and known.

sanskrit: kṣapayitvā tu taṃ kālaṃ gaṇitaṃ kālacoditāḥ sāvaśeṣeṇa kālena saṃbhavanti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Having spent that reckoned span of time, driven on by Time, with a residue of time still remaining they come to birth again and again.

sanskrit: tiryagyonisahasrāṇi gatvā narakam eva ca nirgacchanty avaśā jīvāḥ kālabandhanabandhanāḥ
english: Having passed through thousands of animal wombs and through hell itself, helpless souls emerge again, bound fast in the bondage of Time.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃsaramāṇāni jīvāny aham adṛṣṭavān yathā karma tathā lābha iti śāstranidarśanam
english: Thus have I beheld souls wandering through the round of existence; as is the deed, so is the gain—such is the teaching of the scriptures.

sanskrit: tiryag gacchanti narakaṃ mānuṣyaṃ daivam eva ca sukhaduḥkhe priyadveṣye caritvā pūrvam eva ca
english: They pass into the animal state, into hell, into the human and into the divine, having first lived through pleasure and pain, the loved and the loathed.

sanskrit: kṛtāntavidhisaṃyuktaṃ sarvalokaḥ prapadyate gataṃ gacchanti cādhvānaṃ sarvabhūtāni sarvadā
english: Bound to the ordinance of fate, the whole world goes its way; all beings forever travel the road that has been traveled before.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kālasaṃkhyānasaṃkhyātaṃ sṛṣṭisthitiparāyaṇam taṃ bhāṣamāṇaṃ bhagavān uśanā pratyabhāṣata bhīmān duṣṭapralāpāṃs tvaṃ tāta kasmāt prabhāṣase
english: Bhīṣma said: As he spoke thus of the world bound to the reckoning of Time and devoted to creation and continuance, the venerable Uśanas answered him: "Why, my son, do you utter these dread and perverse ravings?"

sanskrit: vṛtra uvāca pratyakṣam etad bhavatas tathānyeṣāṃ manīṣiṇām mayā yaj jayalubdhena purā taptaṃ mahat tapaḥ
english: Vṛtra said: This is plain before your eyes and before other wise men—the great austerity I once practiced of old, greedy for victory.

sanskrit: gandhān ādāya bhūtānāṃ rasāṃś ca vividhān api avardhaṃ trīn samākramya lokān vai svena tejasā
english: Seizing the fragrances of all beings and their manifold savors as well, I grew mighty, striding across the three worlds by my own splendor.

sanskrit: jvālāmālāparikṣipto vaihāyasacaras tathā ajeyaḥ sarvabhūtānām āsaṃ nityam apetabhīḥ
english: Girt round with garlands of flame, ranging through the air, unconquerable by any being, I was ever free from fear.

sanskrit: aiśvaryaṃ tapasā prāptaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ tac ca svakarmabhiḥ dhṛtim āsthāya bhagavan na śocāmi tatas tv aham
english: The sovereignty I won by austerity was lost again through my own deeds; yet resting upon fortitude, O venerable one, I therefore do not grieve.

sanskrit: yuyutsatā mahendreṇa purā sārdhaṃ mahātmanā tato me bhagavān dṛṣṭo harir nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
english: As of old I longed to do battle with the great-souled Mahendra, then the venerable Lord was revealed to me—Hari, Nārāyaṇa, the sovereign.

sanskrit: vaikuṇṭhaḥ puruṣo viṣṇuḥ śuklo 'nantaḥ sanātanaḥ muñjakeśo hariśmaśruḥ sarvabhūtapitāmahaḥ
english: Vaikuṇṭha, the Person, Viṣṇu, white, infinite, eternal, his hair tawny as muñja-grass, his beard golden, the grandsire of all beings.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ tu tasya tapasaḥ sāvaśeṣaṃ mamāsti vai yad ahaṃ praṣṭum icchāmi bhavantaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam
english: Surely some remnant of that austerity is still mine, since I desire to ask of you the fruit of action.

sanskrit: aiśvaryaṃ vai mahad brahman kasmin varṇe pratiṣṭhitam nivartate cāpi punaḥ katham aiśvaryam uttamam
english: Upon what color, O brahman, does great sovereignty rest? And how does that highest sovereignty again pass away?

sanskrit: kasmād bhūtāni jīvanti pravartante 'tha vā punaḥ kiṃ vā phalaṃ paraṃ prāpya jīvas tiṣṭhati śāśvataḥ
english: From what do beings live, and how again do they come forth into being? And upon attaining what supreme fruit does the soul abide everlasting?

sanskrit: kena vā karmaṇā śakyam atha jñānena kena vā brahmarṣe tat phalaṃ prāptuṃ tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: By what deed, or by what knowledge, O brahman-seer, can that fruit be won? This you should expound to me.

sanskrit: itīdam uktaḥ sa munis tadānīṃ; pratyāha yat tac chṛṇu rājasiṃha mayocyamānaṃ puruṣarṣabha tvam; ananyacittaḥ saha sodarīyaiḥ
english: Thus questioned, that sage made answer then; hear what he said, O lion among kings, O bull among men—as I relate it to you, give it your undivided mind, together with your brothers.

sanskrit: uśanovāca namas tasmai bhagavate devāya prabhaviṣṇave yasya pṛthvītalaṃ tāta sākāśaṃ bāhugocaram
english: Uśanas said: Homage to that venerable God, the all-powerful, within whose arms' reach, my son, lies the surface of the earth together with the sky.

sanskrit: mūrdhā yasya tv anantaṃ ca sthānaṃ dānavasattama tasyāhaṃ te pravakṣyāmi viṣṇor māhātmyam uttamam
english: Whose head is the infinite abode itself, O best of the Dānavas—of him, of Viṣṇu, I shall declare to you the supreme greatness.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tayoḥ saṃvadator evam ājagāma mahāmuniḥ sanatkumāro dharmātmā saṃśayacchedanāya vai
english: Bhīṣma said: As the two conversed thus, there came the great sage Sanatkumāra, righteous of soul, to cut through their doubt.

sanskrit: sa pūjito 'surendreṇa muninośanasā tathā niṣasādāsane rājan mahārhe munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Honored by the lord of the Asuras and likewise by the sage Uśanas, that bull among sages took his seat upon a precious throne, O king.

sanskrit: tam āsīnaṃ mahāprājñam uśanā vākyam abravīt brūhy asmai dānavendrāya viṣṇor māhātmyam uttamam
english: To him seated there, that man of great wisdom, Uśanas spoke these words: "Declare to this lord of the Dānavas the supreme greatness of Viṣṇu."

sanskrit: sanatkumāras tu tataḥ śrutvā prāha vaco 'rthavat viṣṇor māhātmyasaṃyuktaṃ dānavendrāya dhīmate
english: Then Sanatkumāra, having heard, spoke words full of meaning to the wise lord of the Dānavas, words bound up with the greatness of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: śṛṇu sarvam idaṃ daitya viṣṇor māhātmyam uttamam viṣṇau jagat sthitaṃ sarvam iti viddhi paraṃtapa
english: Hear all this, O Daitya—the supreme greatness of Viṣṇu. Know, O scorcher of foes, that the whole universe rests in Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: sṛjaty eṣa mahābāho bhūtagrāmaṃ carācaram eṣa cākṣipate kāle kāle visṛjate punaḥ asmin gacchanti vilayam asmāc ca prabhavanty uta
english: He, O mighty-armed, brings forth the host of beings, moving and unmoving; he withdraws them in their time, and in time sends them forth again. Into him they pass to dissolution, and from him they arise once more.

sanskrit: naiṣa dānavatā śakyas tapasā naiva cejyayā saṃprāptum indriyāṇāṃ tu saṃyamenaiva śakyate
english: He cannot be attained, O Dānava, by austerity nor by sacrifice; only by the restraint of the senses can he be reached.

sanskrit: bāhye cābhyantare caiva karmaṇā manasi sthitaḥ nirmalīkurute buddhyā so 'mutrānantyam aśnute
english: Established in the mind, in both outer and inner action, the man who purifies himself by understanding attains in the world beyond to the infinite.

sanskrit: yathā hiraṇyakartā vai rūpyam agnau viśodhayet bahuśo 'tiprayatnena mahatātmakṛtena ha
english: As the goldsmith refines silver in the fire, many times over and with the greatest effort of his own making,

sanskrit: tadvaj jātiśatair jīvaḥ śudhyate 'lpena karmaṇā yatnena mahatā caivāpy ekajātau viśudhyate
english: so the soul is purified through hundreds of births by little deeds, yet by great effort it may be purified even in a single birth.

sanskrit: līlayālpaṃ yathā gātrāt pramṛjyād ātmano rajaḥ bahu yatnena mahatā doṣanirharaṇaṃ tathā
english: As one may wipe away with ease a little dust from one's own limbs, so by great and abundant effort is the removal of one's faults accomplished.

sanskrit: yathā cālpena mālyena vāsitaṃ tilasarṣapam na muñcati svakaṃ gandhaṃ tadvat sūkṣmasya darśanam
english: And as sesame or mustard, scented with but a little garland, does not release its own scent—such is the perception of what is subtle.

sanskrit: tad eva bahubhir mālyair vāsyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ vimuñcati svakaṃ gandhaṃ mālyagandhe 'vatiṣṭhati
english: But that same seed, perfumed again and again with many garlands, releases its own scent and comes to abide in the fragrance of the garlands.

sanskrit: evaṃ jātiśatair yukto guṇair eva prasaṅgiṣu buddhyā nivartate doṣo yatnenābhyāsajena vai
english: Thus, joined through hundreds of births with the qualities clinging to one, the fault is turned away by understanding, through effort born of repeated practice.

sanskrit: karmaṇā svena raktāni viraktāni ca dānava yathā karmaviśeṣāṃś ca prāpnuvanti tathā śṛṇu
english: By their own deeds beings are colored and discolored, O Dānava; hear now how they attain their particular fortunes according to their works.

sanskrit: yathā ca saṃpravartante yasmiṃs tiṣṭhanti vā vibho tat te 'nupūrvyā vyākhyāsye tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
english: And how they come forth, and in what state they abide, O mighty one—that I shall expound to you in order; listen here with single mind.

sanskrit: anādinidhanaḥ śrīmān harir nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ sa vai sṛjati bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
english: Without beginning or end, glorious, the Lord Hari Nārāyaṇa—he it is who brings forth all beings, the unmoving and the moving alike.

sanskrit: eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu kṣaraś cākṣara eva ca ekādaśavikārātmā jagat pibati raśmibhiḥ
english: He, in all beings, is both the perishable and the imperishable; his nature comprising the eleven modifications, he drinks up the world with his rays.

sanskrit: pādau tasya mahīṃ viddhi mūrdhānaṃ divam eva ca bāhavas tu diśo daitya śrotram ākāśam eva ca
english: Know the earth to be his feet and the heavens his head; the quarters of the sky are his arms, O Daitya, and the firmament his ear.

sanskrit: tasya tejomayaḥ sūryo manaś candramasi sthitam buddhir jñānagatā nityaṃ rasas tv apsu pravartate
english: His radiance is the sun; his mind rests in the moon; his intellect ever abides in knowledge, and his savor flows within the waters.

sanskrit: bhruvor anantarās tasya grahā dānavasattama nakṣatracakraṃ netrābhyāṃ pādayor bhūś ca dānava
english: Between his brows are the planets, O best of the Dānavas; the wheel of constellations springs from his eyes, and the earth from his feet, O Dānava.

sanskrit: rajas tamaś ca sattvaṃ ca viddhi nārāyaṇātmakam so ''śramāṇāṃ mukhaṃ tāta karmaṇas tat phalaṃ viduḥ
english: Know passion, darkness, and goodness to be of Nārāyaṇa's own essence. He is the mouth of all the orders of life, my son, and him they know to be the fruit of action.

sanskrit: akarmaṇaḥ phalaṃ caiva sa eva param avyayaḥ chandāṃsi tasya romāṇi akṣaraṃ ca sarasvatī
english: And the fruit of inaction too is he alone, the supreme and imperishable. The sacred meters are his body-hairs; the imperishable syllable and Sarasvatī are his.

sanskrit: bahvāśrayo bahumukho dharmo hṛdi samāśritaḥ sa brahmaparamo dharmas tapaś ca sad asac ca saḥ
english: Dharma, resting in his heart, has many supports and many faces; he is that dharma whose highest is Brahman, and he is austerity, and the existent and the non-existent both.

sanskrit: śrutiśāstragrahopetaḥ ṣoḍaśartvikkratuś ca saḥ pitāmahaś ca viṣṇuś ca so 'śvinau sa puraṃdaraḥ
english: Endowed with revelation and sacred lore and their grasp, he is the rite of the sixteen priests; he is the Grandsire and Viṣṇu, he is the Aśvins, he is Purandara.

sanskrit: mitraś ca varuṇaś caiva yamo 'tha dhanadas tathā te pṛthagdarśanās tasya saṃvidanti tathaikatām ekasya viddhi devasya sarvaṃ jagad idaṃ vaśe
english: Mitra and Varuṇa, Yama and the Lord of wealth as well—those who see them as distinct know also their oneness in him. Know that all this universe is in the power of that one God.

sanskrit: nānābhūtasya daityendra tasyaikatvaṃ vadaty ayam jantuḥ paśyati jñānena tataḥ sattvaṃ prakāśate
english: Of him who has become manifold, O lord of the Daityas, this teaching declares the oneness; the creature perceives it through knowledge, and then goodness shines forth within.

sanskrit: saṃhāravikṣepasahasrakoṭīs; tiṣṭhanti jīvāḥ pracaranti cānye prajāvisargasya ca pārimāṇyaṃ; vāpīsahasrāṇi bahūni daitya
english: Through thousands of millions of dissolutions and dispersals some souls endure while others wander on; and the measure of the world's emanation, O Daitya, is many thousands of pools.

sanskrit: vāpyaḥ punar yojanavistṛtās tāḥ; krośaṃ ca gambhīratayāvagāḍhāḥ āyāmataḥ pañcaśatāś ca sarvāḥ; pratyekaśo yojanataḥ pravṛddhāḥ
english: Those pools, each a yojana broad, sunk a krośa deep, all five hundred in length, each one extending a full yojana—

sanskrit: vāpyā jalaṃ kṣipyati vālakoṭyā; tv ahnā sakṛc cāpy atha na dvitīyam tāsāṃ kṣaye viddhi kṛtaṃ visargaṃ; saṃhāram ekaṃ ca tathā prajānām
english: from such a pool the water is cast out by the tip of a hair, once in a day and never twice; know that when those pools are emptied, one emanation has been wrought, and likewise one dissolution of beings.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ jīvavarṇāḥ paramaṃ pramāṇaṃ; kṛṣṇo dhūmro nīlam athāsya madhyam raktaṃ punaḥ sahyataraṃ sukhaṃ tu; hāridravarṇaṃ susukhaṃ ca śuklam
english: Six are the colors of souls, by the supreme measure: black, smoky, and blue is its middle; then red, more bearable and bringing ease; yellow, more pleasant still; and white.

sanskrit: paraṃ tu śuklaṃ vimalaṃ viśokaṃ; gataklamaṃ sidhyati dānavendra gatvā tu yoniprabhavāni daitya; sahasraśaḥ siddhim upaiti jīvaḥ
english: But the highest is the white, stainless, sorrowless, and free of weariness—it attains perfection, O lord of the Dānavas. Having passed through wombs of birth by the thousands, O Daitya, the soul comes at last to perfection.

sanskrit: gatiṃ ca yāṃ darśanam āha devo; gatvā śubhaṃ darśanam eva cāha gatiḥ punar varṇakṛtā prajānāṃ; varṇas tathā kālakṛto 'surendra
english: And whatever destiny the God has declared, having reached it, that he has called the auspicious vision; the destiny of beings, in turn, is wrought by their color, and their color, O lord of the Asuras, is wrought by Time.
